title: Amazon and Meta try to hammer out a deal on Muse
hook: 你看見兩個人站在鐵砧兩側，中間一張燒得發亮的合約。
bridge: 接著畫面一轉：一座城堡被護城河圍住，河面上有艘小船想偷偷划過去。
p: The Decoder, citing Fortune, reported that Amazon and Meta are in talks to end Amazon's September block on Meta's AI shopping agent, Muse. The two sides are trying to {0} a deal, but ad revenue and control over search results remain sticking points. Any agreement would need sign-off from both CEOs.

Amazon's ad business brings in $68.6 billion a year, and shopping agents could bypass those ads. That revenue is the {1} Amazon wants to defend. The Decoder, citing Forter Intelligence data, said Muse accounted for 51% of all agentic orders.

words.zh: 艱難地談出協議或細節
words.def: to reach an agreement or work out details after hard negotiation
words.mn: Amazon 和 Meta 的執行長站在鐵砧兩側輪流掄錘，把一張燒紅的合約敲成形，廣告分潤和搜尋排序這兩處凸起慢慢被敲平。一槌槌敲出來，就是談出協議。
words.ex: The union and the airline spent all night trying to hammer out a new contract.
words.exZh: 工會與航空公司整夜努力談出新的合約。

words.zh: 護城河，難以被攻破的競爭優勢
words.def: a lasting advantage that protects a business from competitors
words.mn: Amazon 的廣告城堡外挖了一圈護城河（moat），河裡流的是每年 686 億美元的廣告收入，Muse 的小船想偷偷划過去。擋住來犯者的河，就是競爭優勢。
words.ex: Its huge network of users is the moat that keeps rivals from catching up.
words.exZh: 龐大的用戶網路是讓對手追不上的護城河。

quiz.q: After weeks of talks, the two unions finally ___ a contract.
quiz.why: hammer out 是經過艱難協商談出協議。knock off 是停工或仿冒，talk down 是貶低或勸人冷靜。

quiz.q: Its patented battery technology gives the company a deep ___ that rivals struggle to cross.
quiz.why: moat 是難以被攻破的競爭優勢。bottleneck 是流程中的瓶頸，windfall 是意外之財。
